subject: Biology
title: Endocrine Pancreas: Glucose Homeostasis & Diabetes Mellitus
learningObjectives: Identify pancreatic islet cell types: Alpha (Glucagon), Beta (Insulin), and Delta (Somatostatin)
Explain Insulin hypoglycemic mechanisms (GLUT4 translocation, glycogenesis, lipogenesis)
Contrast Type 1 (IDDM) vs Type 2 (NIDDM) Diabetes Mellitus, including the 3 Polys, Glucosuria, and Ketonuria
content:
The Islets of Langerhans constitute the endocrine pancreas ($\approx 1\text{--}2\text{ Million}$ islets representing $1\text{--}2\%$ of total pancreatic mass).

```
                      PANCREATIC ISLET CELL TYPES
                                   │
         ┌─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┐
         ▼                         ▼                         ▼
   α-CELLS (15–20%)          β-CELLS (70–75%)          δ-CELLS (5%)
   Secretes GLUCAGON         Secretes INSULIN          Secretes SOMATOSTATIN
   (Hyperglycemic Factor)    (Hypoglycemic Factor)     (Inhibits Insulin & Glucagon)
```

### 7.1 Insulin vs. Glucagon Antagonistic Cascade

Normal fasting blood glucose is strictly maintained between **$70\text{ and }110\text{ mg/dL}$**.

```
                   BLOOD GLUCOSE REGULATORY CASCADES
                   
   HYPERGLYCEMIA (High Glucose >110 mg/dL) ──► Pancreatic β-cells release INSULIN
                                                                     │
   Lowers Blood Glucose ◄── Stimulates GLUT4 Glucose Transporters + ──┤
                             Promotes Glycogenesis & Lipogenesis +    │
                             Inhibits Gluconeogenesis ───────────────┘
                             
   HYPOGLYCEMIA (Low Glucose <70 mg/dL)   ──► Pancreatic α-cells release GLUCAGON
                                                                     │
   Raises Blood Glucose ◄── Stimulates Liver Glycogenolysis + ──────┤
                            Promotes Gluconeogenesis & Lipolysis ────┘
```

### 7.2 Diabetes Mellitus Pathophysiology

```
                        DIABETES MELLITUS TYPE COMPARISON
                        
      TYPE 1 DIABETES (IDDM)                    TYPE 2 DIABETES (NIDDM)
      ├── Autoimmune destruction of β-cells     ├── Down-regulation / Resistance of
      ├── Absolute Insulin Deficiency           │   Insulin Receptors
      └── Requires daily insulin injections     └── Relative Insulin Resistance
```

- **Hallmark Manifestations of Diabetes Mellitus**:
  1. **Hyperglycemia**: Abnormally elevated fasting blood glucose ($>126\text{ mg/dL}$).
  2. **Glucosuria**: Excretion of glucose in urine when blood levels exceed the renal threshold ($>180\text{ mg/dL}$).
  3. **Ketonuria**: Formation and urinary excretion of toxic ketone bodies (**Acetoacetate, $\beta$-Hydroxybutyrate, Acetone**) resulting from excessive uninhibited lipolysis.
  4. **The "Three Polys"**: **Polyuria** (frequent urination due to osmotic diuresis), **Polydipsia** (excessive thirst), and **Polyphagia** (excessive hunger).

conceptBreakdown.heading: GLUT4 Translocation Mechanism
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Insulin binds its receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) -> activates IRS-1 -> activates PI3K/Akt pathway -> causes exocytic fusion of intracellular vesicles containing GLUT4 glucose transporters into the plasma membrane of skeletal muscle and adipocytes.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.explanation: In absolute insulin deficiency, hormone-sensitive lipase in adipose tissue becomes hyperactive, flooding the liver with free fatty acids. Accelerated beta-oxidation overwhelms the Krebs cycle, shunting acetyl-CoA into ketogenesis, causing metabolic acidosis and Kussmaul breathing.
